definitions.explanation: Physically demanding or exhausting work. Can also be used figuratively for mentally taxing work that feels overwhelming.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しは{重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう}だ。
{毎日|まいにち}{重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう}で{体|からだ}がボロボロだ。
examples.english: My body is falling apart from heavy labor every day.

examples.japanese: {介護|かいご}の{仕事|しごと}は{精神的|せいしんてき}にも{肉体的|にくたいてき}にも{重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Caregiving work is said to be hard labor both mentally and physically.

notes:
USAGE:
Can describe literal heavy physical work or be used figuratively for any extremely demanding task. Often used emphatically in everyday conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう}を{強|し}いられる (to be forced into hard labor)
- {重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう}に{耐|た}える (to endure hard labor)
- {肉体的|にくたいてき}な{重|じゅう}{労働|ろうどう} (physically demanding labor)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {肉体|にくたい}{労働|ろうどう}: physical labor — emphasizes it being bodily work, not necessarily exhausting
- {過重|かじゅう}{労働|ろうどう}: overwork — excessive work hours, a social issue in Japan
